# Model 3 (Categorical Variables)

Some variables that I wanted to include in the second model were categorical and couldn't be processed using the same method. I tried only categorical variables and the RMSE was significantly worse than the numeric only version.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

# Read data
data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')

# Encode categorical variables
X = pd.get_dummies(data.drop(['customer_id', 'monthly_spend', 'age', 'num_children', 'credit_score', 'owns_home', 'annual_income', 'has_auto_loan', 'num_credit_cards', 'credit_limit', 'num_transactions', 'tenure', 'avg_transaction_value', 'reward_points_balance', 'travel_frequency', 'online_shopping_freq', 'utility_payment_count'], axis=1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)
y = data.monthly_spend

reg = LinearRegression()
reg.fit(X,y)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X = pd.get_dummies(scoring_data.drop(['customer_id'], axis=1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)
scoring_X = scoring_X.reindex(columns=X.columns, fill_value=0)
pred = reg.predict(scoring_X)

# Construct submission
submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': pred})
submission_file.to_csv('../PACFiles/submission_file_4.csv', index=False)

from sklearn.metrics import root_mean_squared_error
train_pred = reg.predict(X)
rmse = root_mean_squared_error(y, train_pred)
print("Training RMSE:", rmse)
```
